class.name: NetwPredictWritePlan
class.brief_description: The recovery staged for one authoritative comparison: the state to restore, the row to publish, and whether either is owed at all.
class.description: A recovery mutates the engine's own dense state and separately publishes the same values as a row a shell can drain. [method restore_at] and [method restore_has] answer what was written into the engine's state directly. [method write_at] and [method write_has] answer the published copy: a shell drains it onto its bound nodes, while a shell-less driver reads the engine state instead and leaves it undrained. The two agree in value whenever both are present, and exist separately because they serve two different readers. [br][br][method skip] is [code]true[/code] by default and stays [code]true[/code] whenever no recovery was owed for this comparison; every other member then answers its zero default rather than a real plan. [codeblock] if plan.skip(): return for field in range(field_count): if plan.restore_has(field): engine_state[field] = plan.restore_at(field) if plan.write_has(field): node.set(field_name, plan.write_at(field)) [/codeblock]

method.name: basis
method.description: The transition this plan's correction was computed against, or [code]-1[/code] when [method skip] is [code]true[/code].

method.name: escalated
method.description: Whether this correction escalated to a stronger policy than the one already in effect. A caller that sees this [code]true[/code] closes out any still-pending write on the episode as a non-contraction rather than waiting for its own verify run to elapse, since an escalation means that pending write was superseded before it could settle.

method.name: operator_kind
method.description: The [enum NetwPredictJournal.Operator] this plan applies, meaningless while [method skip] is [code]true[/code].

method.name: replay_from
method.description: The oldest transition this plan owes a replay from, or [code]-1[/code] when it owes no replay. Set only under replay-mode correction, where the restore alone is not enough to bring the state back in sync.

method.name: replay_through
method.description: The newest transition this plan's replay covers, or [code]-1[/code] when it owes no replay.

method.name: restore_at
method.description: The value this plan writes into the engine's own state for [param field], meaningless unless [method restore_has] is [code]true[/code] for the same field.

method.name: restore_has
method.description: Whether this plan's engine-state restore captured [param field] at all. A restore is sparse, so a field this answers [code]false[/code] for is left untouched.

method.name: skip
method.description: Whether this plan owes no correction at all. When [code]true[/code], every other member answers its zero default rather than a real value, and a caller returns without touching state.

method.name: teleport
method.description: Whether this plan's restore is a discontinuous teleport rather than a value a caller may blend toward smoothly.

method.name: write_at
method.description: The value this plan publishes for a shell to drain onto [param field]'s bound node, meaningless unless [method write_has] is [code]true[/code] for the same field.

method.name: write_has
method.description: Whether this plan's published row captured [param field] at all. Sparse in the same way as [method restore_has], and usually true for exactly the same fields.
